items.headline: Brent jumps 3.1% to $116.72, its highest settlement since April, on Houthi attacks across Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Attacks hit Saudi energy infrastructure and the kingdom's state oil producer evacuated its Dhahran headquarters; an oil spill off the UAE added to supply fears. Brent touched $117.45. Up from about $109–110 earlier this week. Escalating sharply.
items.rationale: Crude near $117 sharply widens India's import bill, lifts fuel, freight and input costs and adds to inflation already at 5.5% retail and 11.4% wholesale, while pressuring the rupee and reserves.

items.headline: Iran says 7 oil tankers were hit in one night in Hormuz; October attacks reach a record
items.summary: Iran is using new tactics aimed at keeping oil prices high, and an oil slick threatens the strait after a tanker attack. Fears of a return to full war are growing. Escalating.
items.rationale: More attacks on India's main crude and LNG route keep insurance, freight and delivered energy costs at records.

items.headline: Sensex falls for a fourth day to 73,123.83; midcaps drop 2.21% and smallcaps 2.94% as crude tops $114
items.summary: Nifty slipped 0.39% to 22,600; the volatility index rose 6%. Losses narrowed late in the session. Broader markets fell far more than large caps. Escalating.
items.rationale: Surging crude hits smaller, cost-sensitive companies hardest; the volatility jump shows rising risk aversion.

items.headline: Foreign investors buy a net ₹888 crore; domestic funds add ₹3,235 crore
items.summary: A rare buying day for foreign funds, though they still hold about 2.8 lakh net short index futures contracts. Domestic institutions have bought for several sessions. Tentative easing.
items.rationale: Any sustained foreign buying would support banks and the rupee, but large short positions show caution remains.

items.headline: Forex reserves fall $5.01 billion to $721.02 billion, a sixth straight weekly drop
items.summary: In the week to 16 October, foreign currency assets fell $5.76 billion while gold rose $0.71 billion. Reserves are about $65 billion below the September record. Smaller fall than the prior $8.58 billion. Ongoing.
items.rationale: Continued drawdown shows the cost of defending the rupee; oil at $117 will add to dollar demand.

items.headline: Drone strike sinks a cargo ship in the Black Sea, 1 dead; Ukraine proposes a Turkey–India–Egypt grain corridor
items.summary: Romania blamed Russia. The European Parliament called for an EU naval operation, and Germany warned the attacks raise the risk of global famine. Escalating.
items.rationale: Collapsing Black Sea exports keep world wheat, sunflower oil and fertiliser prices high; a corridor involving India could ease supply.

items.headline: Nigeria raises LNG exports to India since the Iran war began
items.summary: Adds to Oman and other non-Hormuz suppliers replacing lost Gulf cargoes. Ongoing diversification.
items.rationale: Non-Gulf LNG reduces physical shortage risk for fertiliser, city gas and power, though prices stay high.

items.headline: Record crude shipping costs keep fuel price relief away for Indian consumers
items.summary: Freight on Russian and other crude to India is at records, offsetting discounts. With Brent at $117, pump price cuts look unlikely. Ongoing.
items.rationale: Unchanged or higher fuel prices keep transport and household costs up and squeeze state fuel retailers' margins.
